topic.subject: social
topic.title: Panchayati Raj and local government
topic.scope: Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, sarpanch, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad, urban local bodies, ward councillors

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Sabha consists only of the elected members of the Panchayat.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the executive body with the general assembly of voters.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Sabha includes every person in the village who is 18 years or older and on the voters' list.

probe.question: Who attends the Gram Sabha meeting?
probe.wrong_answer: Only the Sarpanch and the Ward members.

misconceptions.root_belief: Only leaders participate in government decisions.

misconceptions.statement: The Sarpanch has absolute power to make all village decisions alone.
misconceptions.why: Students equate the Sarpanch with a monarch or a single boss.
misconceptions.fix: The Sarpanch works with the Gram Panchayat members and is accountable to the Gram Sabha.

probe.question: Can the Sarpanch decide to build a road without asking anyone?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because he is the head of the village.

misconceptions.statement: The Zila Parishad makes laws for the whole country.
misconceptions.why: Students overgeneralize the term 'Parishad' or 'Council' to national levels.
misconceptions.fix: The Zila Parishad operates at the district level and coordinates activities of the Panchayat Samitis.

probe.question: What is the scope of the Zila Parishad?
probe.wrong_answer: It is the highest law-making body in India.

misconceptions.statement: Ward councillors are appointed by the government, not elected.
misconceptions.why: Students assume local urban officials are bureaucrats rather than representatives.
misconceptions.fix: Ward councillors are elected representatives chosen by the people living in that specific ward.

probe.question: How does a person become a ward councillor?
probe.wrong_answer: They are selected by the city mayor or government officials.

misconceptions.root_belief: Government officials are always appointed by superiors.

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Panchayat builds and runs the village's roads, school and hospital entirely by itself with no outside help.
misconceptions.why: Students see the Panchayat as the only local authority and ignore its links to higher bodies and government schemes.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Panchayat looks after local work like drinking water, street lights, roads and sanitation, but it works with Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad and government grants.

probe.question: Who provides all the money and builds the village school and hospital?
probe.wrong_answer: The Gram Panchayat alone does everything without any help.

misconceptions.root_belief: Local body works alone, independent of other levels

misconceptions.statement: The Panchayat Samiti is the body at the district level above the Zila Parishad.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the order of the three tiers and think bigger names mean lower or higher levels wrongly.
misconceptions.fix: The three tiers are Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block) and Zila Parishad (district), the highest tier.

probe.question: Which is the highest body of the Panchayati Raj system: Panchayat Samiti or Zila Parishad?
probe.wrong_answer: Panchayat Samiti is at the top because it covers the district.

misconceptions.root_belief: Hierarchy order of tiers is arbitrary or reversed

misconceptions.statement: A ward councillor looks after the whole city and not just one ward.
misconceptions.why: Students think the word councillor means a city head, not the representative of a small area.
misconceptions.fix: A ward councillor is elected by the people of one ward, a small part of the town or city, and speaks for the problems of that ward in the council.

probe.question: Whom should a family in Ward 5 meet about a broken drain in their lane?
probe.wrong_answer: The councillor of the whole city, since he looks after every area.

misconceptions.root_belief: Representatives cover entire area, not a constituency

misconceptions.statement: Only men who own land in the village can attend and vote in the Gram Sabha.
misconceptions.why: Students carry over social stereotypes about who counts in village decisions.
misconceptions.fix: All adult men and women in the village who are on the voter list (18 years or older) are members of the Gram Sabha, whether or not they own land.

probe.question: Can a woman who owns no land and works as a labourer attend the Gram Sabha?
probe.wrong_answer: No, only landowning men can attend the Gram Sabha.

misconceptions.root_belief: Only property-owning men have a say in decisions

misconceptions.statement: The Sarpanch is appointed by the district collector and not chosen by villagers.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the Sarpanch with government officers like the collector or the village secretary.
misconceptions.fix: The Sarpanch is the head of the Gram Panchayat, chosen through election by the villagers (in the Panchayat's ward members' elections), not appointed by an officer.

probe.question: How does a person become Sarpanch of a village?
probe.wrong_answer: The collector selects and appoints him.

misconceptions.root_belief: Local leaders are appointed by government officials

misconceptions.statement: Panchayat funds come only from the pocket money of the Sarpanch and members.
misconceptions.why: Students think of money as personal and do not know about taxes, grants and schemes.
misconceptions.fix: Panchayat funds come from local taxes and fees, and grants from the state and central governments, used for public works.

probe.question: Where does the Panchayat get money to repair the village well?
probe.wrong_answer: From the personal money of the Sarpanch.

misconceptions.root_belief: Public money equals leader's personal money

misconceptions.statement: The Zila Parishad looks after the problems of a single village like a broken lane.
misconceptions.why: Students think the highest rural body handles all matters, including tiny local ones.
misconceptions.fix: The Zila Parishad works at the district level, planning and coordinating development across many blocks and villages; village matters are handled by the Gram Panchayat.

probe.question: Who should first handle a small drainage problem in one village?
probe.wrong_answer: The Zila Parishad, since it is the biggest body.

misconceptions.root_belief: Higher bodies handle every small local issue

misconceptions.statement: Municipal Corporation and Municipal Council are the same, and both are found in villages.
misconceptions.why: Students treat similar-sounding words as synonyms and forget the rural-urban divide.
misconceptions.fix: Municipal Corporations govern big cities and Municipal Councils govern smaller towns; villages have Gram Panchayats instead.

probe.question: Which body governs a big city like Mumbai: Gram Panchayat or Municipal Corporation?
probe.wrong_answer: Both are the same and run villages.
